verdicts.verdict_one_line: Grounding in E1 is precise (income -0.76% over six months, stable 3.0% savings rate, April dip, stronger-than-expected May) and it honestly notes 'The specific percentage growth for May 2026 is not provided', but it books all three paths as CONTRADICTED while reporting 'Structural use facts: 3 of 3 routed paths contributed... Directional conflict is absent.' and still leans on their downward effects to place a 0.2% central and 0.65 on 'no' after calling magnitude support unsupported.

ranking_rationale: The separator was whether the trace let the 0.07pp distance between the last observed print and the 0.974% boundary govern its confidence: principle_memory and direct_forecast anchored on cited figures and kept mass modest, while structure_memory turned 'close to the threshold' into a 0.70 bet on crossing it and case_memory produced no question-specific content at all. Middle traces (factor_memory, structured_reasoning, hgf) were well grounded in their own banks but each declared magnitude support insufficient and then hardened the distribution anyway.
shared_evidence_note: Partly both: the E1 traces (factor_memory, hgf) genuinely never saw the 0.9% May or 1.7% March figures that anchored the E0 traces and correctly said so, yet within E0 itself structure_memory reached 'yes' and the other four reached 'no' from the identical 0.9% print, so the sharpest disagreement is one of reasoning, not evidence.
